title: Conditional logic in a function
description: PL/pgSQL functions can use IF/ELSIF/ELSE, just like the CASE expression you've already used, but as full procedural control flow. Create a function `price_tier(price NUMERIC) RETURNS TEXT` that returns `'budget'` if price is under 20, `'mid'` if price is 20 to 50 inclusive, and `'premium'` otherwise.
hints: 💡 SQL concept to consider: IF / ELSIF / ELSE, PL/pgSQL
IF price < 20 THEN RETURN 'budget'; ELSIF price <= 50 THEN RETURN 'mid'; ELSE RETURN 'premium'; END IF; - each branch RETURNs directly instead of building up a value to return at the end.

CREATE FUNCTION price_tier(price NUMERIC) RETURNS TEXT AS $$ BEGIN IF ... THEN RETURN ...; ELSIF ... THEN RETURN ...; ELSE RETURN ...; END IF; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql - fill in each condition and return value yourself.
expected_behavior: price_tier(15) returns 'budget', price_tier(35) returns 'mid', price_tier(80) returns 'premium'.
solution: CREATE FUNCTION price_tier(price NUMERIC) RETURNS TEXT AS $$ BEGIN IF price < 20 THEN RETURN 'budget'; ELSIF price <= 50 THEN RETURN 'mid'; ELSE RETURN 'premium'; END IF; END; $$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;
explanation: Notice this needs its own END IF; to close the IF block, separate from the END; that closes the whole function body - PL/pgSQL's block-ending keywords always come in matching pairs like that.
